## Per-claim detail

### Claim 1 — Option E uniqueness enforcement (load-bearing per §D63.5)

**Verdict:** PASS

**Evidence:**

(a) Migration 0019 carries a NON-UNIQUE index, with the partial-UNIQUE limitation documented in the comment block above it.

`/root/projects/phi/baby-phi/modules/crates/store/migrations/0019_agent_profile_n_to_1_schema.surql:96-105`:
```sql
-- Index `blueprint_agent_id` is a NON-UNIQUE read-side lookup index
-- supporting efficient `SELECT * FROM blueprint WHERE agent_id = $aid`
-- queries used by the per-agent override read path. The 1:1 override-
-- row-per-agent uniqueness constraint is enforced at the REPOSITORY
-- TIER (`upsert_agent_blueprint_override` in `repo_impl.rs`) inside a
-- SurrealDB `BEGIN; ... COMMIT;` transaction — SurrealDB 2.6.5 does NOT
-- support filtered/partial UNIQUE indexes (`DEFINE INDEX ... UNIQUE WHERE ...`
-- is rejected by the parser). See ADR-0063 §D63.5 + §D63.12 for the
-- application-tier enforcement rationale + the half-migrated runtime
-- tolerance cross-reference.
```

`/root/projects/phi/baby-phi/modules/crates/store/migrations/0019_agent_profile_n_to_1_schema.surql:118-120`:
```sql
DEFINE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS blueprint_agent_id
    ON blueprint
    FIELDS agent_id;
```

Confirmed: NO `UNIQUE` keyword (NOT `... FIELDS agent_id UNIQUE`).

(b) `upsert_agent_blueprint_override` wraps its work in a SurrealDB transaction (`BEGIN TRANSACTION; ... COMMIT TRANSACTION;`).

`/root/projects/phi/baby-phi/modules/crates/store/src/repo_impl.rs:905-955` carries the trait impl. Body excerpt at 933-944:
```rust
self.client()
    .query(
        "BEGIN TRANSACTION; \
         DELETE blueprint WHERE agent_id = $agent AND id != type::thing('blueprint', $id); \
         UPSERT type::thing('blueprint', $id) CONTENT $body RETURN NONE; \
         LET $a = type::thing('agent', $agent); \
         LET $b = type::thing('blueprint', $id); \
         DELETE agent_uses_blueprint_override WHERE in = $a; \
         RELATE $a -> agent_uses_blueprint_override -> $b \
            SET id = type::thing('agent_uses_blueprint_override', $edge) \
            RETURN NONE; \
         COMMIT TRANSACTION;",
    )
```

Note: the implementation uses a `DELETE`-then-`UPSERT` pattern rather than a separate `SELECT`-then-`UPDATE`. The `DELETE blueprint WHERE agent_id = $agent AND id != type::thing('blueprint', $id)` clause evicts any stale override rows for the same agent before the UPSERT lands the new canonical row. Functionally equivalent to the audit-prompt-asserted "SELECTs any existing override row + UPSERT": both achieve the 1:1-override-row-per-agent invariant transactionally. The audit-prompt wording uses "SELECT" semantically — the actual implementation uses the more efficient DELETE-then-UPSERT inside the same BEGIN/COMMIT transaction, which is a superior pattern (single-pass, no read-before-write race).

PASS — load-bearing semantic preserved (single transaction enforcing 1:1-override-per-agent).
